parameters.content:
## Price Ingestion Agent
Receipt half of price ingestion (the Price Refresh Agent covers the other half: scheduled live web-scrape refreshes for items not recently repurchased). Reuses the same dedicated household Telegram bot as Check-In/Budget Alert — send it a photo of a receipt, it extracts every line item via vision LLM and writes them straight into Catalog + PriceLog with confidence: receipt, no 24-48h staging hold, since a receipt is a real observed purchase (ground truth), not an estimate.

Same structured-JSON-only extraction discipline as the Price Refresh Agent (CLAUDE.md §5, 'never free text'). New items (never before in Catalog) are created via appendOrUpdate rather than the Price Refresh Agent's plain update, since a receipt can introduce a first-time item.

SUB-WORKFLOW, not its own Telegram trigger: n8n only allows one Telegram Trigger per bot, and Check-In Reply Listener already owns it. This workflow is invoked via Execute Workflow from a new 'Has Photo?' branch added to Check-In Reply Listener (before its existing Parse Reply node), which forwards the raw { message } object unchanged — so everything downstream here still reads $json.message.* exactly as if this were still a direct trigger.

STATUS: built 2026-08-09, not yet wired with real credentials or live-tested — needs the same live-application pass as every other agent in this project (Google Sheets credential, Anthropic credential, real spreadsheet ID, and wiring the calling branch into Check-In Reply Listener).

nodes.name: Called by Check-In Reply Listener
nodes.notes: Entry point when Check-In Reply Listener's 'Has Photo?' branch forwards a photo message here via Execute Workflow — see Setup Notes. Receives { message } shaped identically to a raw Telegram Trigger output, so 'Has Photo?' below can still be a genuine defensive re-check rather than blind trust of the caller.

parameters.text: Send a photo of your receipt and I'll log the prices — the whole receipt in one shot is fine, no need to crop per item.

nodes.name: Download Receipt Photo
nodes.notes: Downloads the actual image bytes as binary (n8n's Telegram node resolves file_id → file_path → download internally, so the bot token never needs to be handled directly in this workflow). Binary lands on the default 'data' property.

nodes.name: Encode Photo as Base64
nodes.notes: Fixed 2026-08-09 live: n8n Cloud uses filesystem-backed binary storage, so $binary.data.data evaluates to undefined in expressions (silently dropped by JSON serialization — Anthropic returned 'field required'). this.helpers.getBinaryDataBuffer() is the storage-agnostic way to get the actual bytes; referenced downstream as $json.imageBase64.

nodes.name: Extract Receipt via LLM
nodes.notes: Structured-JSON-only extraction, same discipline as the Price Refresh Agent's 'Extract Price via LLM' (CLAUDE.md §5). Vision content block references the downloaded photo's base64 binary directly — same anthropic-version header requirement already confirmed live 2026-07-31 on the Price Refresh Agent.

parameters.text: Couldn't read that receipt clearly — could you try again with a flatter, better-lit photo? Cropping out anything but the item lines and totals can help too.

nodes.name: Log Extraction Failure
nodes.notes: On Error set to Continue live 2026-08-09 -- once web-upload triggered runs started sharing this false-branch, an unhandled Telegram error here (chatId is undefined for web-triggered runs, since Pick Largest Photo never ran) would otherwise abort the whole execution, including the parallel Format Web Error Response branch.

nodes.name: Split Items
nodes.notes: One output item per receipt line, so each can be upserted into Catalog and appended to PriceLog independently below.

nodes.name: Upsert Item into Catalog
nodes.notes: appendOrUpdate (not the Price Refresh Agent's plain update) since a receipt can introduce a first-time item never before in Catalog — matched on item+store, same compound key the Price Refresh Agent uses. unit_price is deliberately left blank here rather than computed, since a receipt-printed size alone isn't enough to safely derive it without risking the exact kind of unverified cross-store comparison CLAUDE.md's caution-icon convention exists to prevent — leave that to manual entry or a future pass.

nodes.name: Append to PriceLog
nodes.notes: Always a plain append — PriceLog is append-only history (schema doc), never matched/overwritten. status: receipt distinguishes these ground-truth rows from the Price Refresh Agent's pending/promoted scrape rows at a glance.

nodes.name: Format Confirmation Message
nodes.notes: alwaysOutputData not needed here since Validate Extraction already guaranteed items.length > 0 before this branch was ever reached.

nodes.name: Send Confirmation
nodes.notes: On Error set to Continue live, same safety pattern used on every other Telegram send in this project (Send Finalize Summary etc.) so a Telegram hiccup can never take down the ingestion itself — the sheet writes above have already succeeded by this point regardless. Also required now that web-uploaded receipts share this branch: chatId is undefined for web-triggered runs (Pick Largest Photo never ran), which would otherwise abort the whole execution.

nodes.name: Web Upload Trigger
nodes.notes: Second entry point, added 2026-08-09 for direct in-app receipt upload (camera or file picker) -- lets the PWA POST a receipt straight to this workflow instead of going through Telegram. No auth on this endpoint (same trust model as the List/Budget webhook, URL obscurity only). Expected body: { imageBase64: string, mediaType: string }. Response mode is 'Using Respond to Webhook Node' so the app gets a synchronous JSON result once the sheet writes are done, not just an immediate ack.

nodes.name: Normalize Web Upload
nodes.notes: Feeds directly into Extract Receipt via LLM (fan-in, same target the Telegram path's Encode Photo as Base64 also feeds) -- output shape matches what that node's Encode Photo as Base64 counterpart produces.

nodes.name: Respond to Webhook (Error)
nodes.notes: On Error: Continue -- this node is a no-op when the run came from Telegram (no pending webhook call to respond to).

nodes.name: Respond to Webhook (Success)
nodes.notes: On Error: Continue -- this node is a no-op when the run came from Telegram (no pending webhook call to respond to).
